thesis: SoundHound is doubling down on scale-by-acquisition: record Q1 2026 revenue of $44.2M (+52% y/y) but a $25.0M GAAP net loss at just 31.1% gross margin, now merging all-stock with LivePerson (itself lossmaking) to target a combined $500M revenue run-rate with 25 of the Fortune 100 as customers. FY2026 guidance is $225-260M and 2027 $350-400M including LivePerson. With $216M cash, no debt, and adjusted EBITDA of -$26.7M per quarter, the equity at ~$2.8B (~12x forward sales) is a bet that two unprofitable conversational-AI companies become one profitable one before the cash and patience run out.
catalysts: LivePerson merger close expected 2H 2026; integration milestones and combined guidance
FY2026 guidance $225-260M reaffirmed; 2027 guided $350-400M including LivePerson
Path-to-EBITDA-breakeven commentary (scale thesis) at upcoming quarters
Fortune 100 penetration (25 of 100 post-merger) converting to expansion revenue
risk_factors: Two lossmakers merging: SoundHound has never been profitable and is acquiring a company that also loses money - integration cost and noncash volatility flagged in coverage
Gross margin 31.1% is software-in-name-only economics (voice compute costs); the scale thesis requires margin structure to transform, not just revenue to add
Cash runway: $216M against ~$26.7M/quarter adjusted-EBITDA burn plus acquisition expenses - roughly two years before dilution risk returns
Beta 4.16 - the most volatile name on the watchlist; +2.26% week masks violent daily swings (+5.79% on merger day)
Big-tech competition (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI voice/agentic stacks) with infinite balance sheets

q1_2026_revenue.note: +52% y/y, record; GAAP net loss 25.0M; GM 31.1%; adj EBITDA -26.7M

liveperson_deal.note: all-stock; LivePerson debt eliminated; combined $500M revenue target; close 2H 2026
